questions.question: Plants make their own food using sunlight in a process called ___.
questions.funFact: Plants are the only living things that can make their own food using sunlight, water and air.

questions.question: Which part of a plant takes in water from the soil?
questions.funFact: Roots also hold the plant firmly in the ground so it does not fall over in the wind.

questions.question: Which part of a plant usually makes the food?
questions.funFact: Leaves are like tiny kitchens where the plant cooks its food using sunlight.

questions.question: Plants give out oxygen, which humans need to breathe.
questions.funFact: This is why growing more trees helps give us cleaner, fresher air.

questions.question: The green colour in leaves comes from a substance called ___.
questions.funFact: Chlorophyll is what captures sunlight so the plant can use its energy to make food.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a part of a plant?
questions.funFact: Gills are body parts that fish use to breathe underwater, not parts of a plant.

questions.question: Match each plant part to the job it does.
questions.funFact: Every part of a plant has an important job that keeps the whole plant alive.

questions.question: A cactus stores water in its thick stem to survive in the desert.
questions.funFact: A cactus has sharp spines instead of leaves, which helps it lose less water in the hot desert.

questions.question: A young plant grows out of a ___.
questions.funFact: A seed carries a tiny baby plant inside it, waiting for water and warmth to start growing.

questions.question: Which of these plants can trap and eat insects?
questions.funFact: The Venus flytrap snaps its leaves shut in a flash to catch insects that land on it.

questions.question: Which gas do plants take from the air to make their food?
questions.funFact: Plants take in the carbon dioxide that we breathe out, which helps keep the air balanced.

questions.question: The stem holds up the plant and carries water to the leaves.
questions.funFact: The stem works like a set of tiny pipes carrying water and food around the plant.
